A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Air-DualODE and retain matching methods, experiments and appendices. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison, including v2's expanded appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original PM2.5 forecasting experiments on Beijing and KnowAir, including baseline comparisons, component ablations and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds forecasting breakdowns, solver and hyperparameter studies, fusion ablations and case analyses.

M1.justification: BA-DAE, the masked-attention data branch, Decay-TCL, GNN fusion and the combined objective are retained. Explicit vector notation for beta clarifies the station-specific correction already described and visualized in v1. Appendix A.14 elaborates the data-branch architecture already shown in Figure 2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PM2.5 forecasting on Beijing's 35 stations and KnowAir's 184 cities, including sudden changes. The additional forecast breakdowns and case studies use this existing coverage; other domains are discussed only as future applications.

E2.justification: V2 adds MTSF-DG to Table 1's standard and sudden-change comparisons on both datasets. All previously evaluated baseline methods remain. The added method is an actual results row, not merely a new citation.

E3.justification: Existing splits, preprocessing and the 72-hour input/output protocol are retained. New studies vary GNN depth and loss weight, compare Euler, RK4 and Dopri5 with whole-test-set inference timing, and introduce fusion controls including an MLP with matched layer count. These extend evaluation without revising the original benchmark protocol.

E4.justification: V2 adds convergence curves, hyperparameter and solver sensitivity studies, GNN-versus-MLP/pooling fusion ablations, KnowAir and advection-graph visualizations, and sudden-change failure cases. Appendix A.17 also reports instability after removing layer normalization. These substantially expand testing of design choices, robustness and failure conditions beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. The added sensitivity and convergence plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, including Air-DualODE's overall MAEs of 40.32 and 18.64. V2 adds MTSF-DG results, daily-window and individual-step errors, solver accuracy/runtime results, fusion-ablation scores and qualitative failure findings. For example, new Table 6 reports Beijing inference times of 0.9 seconds for Euler and 1.98 for Dopri5; these compare solver settings, not versions.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 newly states the explicit requirement lambda1 > lambda2 for Decay-TCL. The diffusion/advection derivations and conservation proof in Appendices A.2–A.3 remain substantively unchanged. Vector beta notation and consolidation of the loss equations are clarifications rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: open-system BA-DAE, aligned and fused dual dynamics, and state-of-the-art city- and national-scale prediction. The physics-informed-to-physics-guided terminology change does not redefine these contributions; new failure qualifications concern limitations.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications absent from v1: missed sudden-change peaks, possible inadequacy of the current sudden-change evaluation, dependence on layer normalization with Dopri5, and required physical-branch adaptation for other domains. It also interprets fusion alternatives through neighboring versus distant-station information and discusses solver accuracy/runtime tradeoffs.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and Appendix A.14's explicit projection, residual-attention and normalization equations. New studies document parameter ranges, fusion controls and the timing scope. Appendix A.7's hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch size and default solver settings are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository accessibility.

R1.justification: V2 adds neural diffusion/advection and reaction-diffusion references, among other citations supporting its expanded discussion. Appendix A.17 and Table 8 explicitly contrast Air-DualODE with AirPhyNet, including architecture and claimed efficiency. These elaborate the existing positioning without replacing the central open-system and dual-dynamics novelty claims.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. V2 changes terminology, rewrites the conclusion, clarifies notation, adds acknowledgments and cross-references, and organizes new material into appendix subsections. This is limited editing of the existing narrative rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4–8 for forecast breakdowns, solver results, fusion ablations and method comparison, plus Figures 8–12 for convergence, sensitivity, spatial cases and prediction failures. Existing main figures and tables are largely retained, with an added Table 1 row and small diagram/notation edits.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for previously under-tested design choices through fusion controls and solver studies (Tables 6–7). Its sudden-change examples and explicit stability and generalization limitations also make applicability more assessable. These gains outweigh reporting defects, including the unresolved equation reference, MAPE/SMAPE label inconsistency and unquantified AirPhyNet speed claim. The improvement concerns validation and transparency, not higher same-setting prediction scores.
